blogs.title: The Dog Bite That Almost Killed: Recognizing Capnocytophaga Sepsis
blogs.description: A review of Capnocytophaga canimorsus, a rare but fulminant zoonosis associated with dog bites. We discuss the rapid progression to septic shock and DIC, the importance of empiric penicillin coverage in bite wounds, and risk factors in immunocompetent hosts.

blogs.title: Sepsis, DIC, or TMA? Untangling the Coagulopathy Web
blogs.description: Distinguishing sepsis-induced coagulopathy from thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) is a critical ICU challenge. This post analyzes the timeline of hemolysis, schistocytes, and platelet counts to differentiate DIC from superimposed TMA in the context of severe infection.

blogs.title: Normal Complement Levels Do Not Rule Out HUS: The CM-HUS Diagnostic Trap
blogs.description: Clinicians often rule out complement-mediated HUS based on normal C3/C4 levels. This post explains why standard complement panels can be misleading, the role of kidney biopsy in confirming TMA, and the importance of exclusion criteria for TTP and STEC-HUS.

blogs.title: To Block or Not to Block: Eculizumab in the Setting of Active Bacteraemia
blogs.description: Eculizumab is the standard treatment for CM-HUS but carries a risk of overwhelming infection with encapsulated organisms. We discuss the timing of initiation relative to infection clearance, the necessity of meningococcal vaccination, and antibiotic prophylaxis strategies.

blogs.title: Refractory Hypoglycemia in Sepsis: A Red Flag for Capnocytophaga
blogs.description: Severe, refractory hypoglycemia is a specific and often overlooked marker of severe Capnocytophaga sepsis. This post highlights the metabolic derangements associated with this pathogen and why it should prompt immediate broad-spectrum coverage in bite wound patients.
